title: Planning a Meal
instructions: Speak about a real or imagined shared meal, then use feedback to improve the recording.
prompt: Describe a real or imagined meal you plan with someone. Say what food you want, where you will prepare it, one item to buy, and a polite question about a drink. Explain one choice. Speak for about 75–105 seconds. Compare two food choices and explain whether quantities are enough or too much.
reference: I plan a shared meal with a friend in a bright kitchen. We want to cook rice and vegetables because both of us enjoy them. I will check a recipe before we start and put a clean bowl on the table. We need to buy some fruit and an egg. I can ask my friend, “Would you like tea or coffee after the meal?” If my friend is late, I will send a message and wait before we begin cooking. I prefer the easier recipe because it has fewer steps. Two eggs are enough for us; six would be too many. We choose the fresher apples and use a bigger bowl to mix the food. This helps us prepare a meal without buying more than we need.
